solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A Hindu deity, not very apparent in area around China?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'not' asks for the letter V, the abbreviation of very, to be removed from the deity

parts.note: Siva (Shiva) is the Hindu god of destruction

explanation.surface: A Hindu god proves hard to spot somewhere in the region of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' asks for the abbreviation V to go; Siva is the usual crossword spelling of Shiva.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent containing China is the region around it, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Blood, litre filling mark of cut

indicators.note: filling means the litre letter goes inside the mark, packing it

parts.note: a caret is the proofreader's mark showing where text was cut or must be inserted

explanation.surface: A litre of blood spilling from a wound left by a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts L inside CARET.
explanation.definitionFit: In old boxing slang red wine named after Bordeaux stands for blood, from its deep red colour.

clue.text: Specify type of wheat cut by hooligan

indicators.note: cut means the wheat word loses its tail letter

parts.note: spelt is an ancient variety of wheat
a lout is a rough, uncouth young man, a hooligan

explanation.surface: Instructions to name a grain variety that a vandal has trampled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims SPELT to SPEL, which is then followed 'by' LOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something out explicitly and in detail is to specify it; a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Inventory expert changing tack, having 15 round about

indicators.note: round about means the writer's name goes around the reworked letters

parts.note: points to the solution of 15 across, the sensational writer

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of tack are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A stock-checker who switches tack while a furnace worker hovers about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' signals the anagram and 'round about' the container; '15' is a cross-reference to the writer at 15 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who counts goods held in a shop or warehouse is an inventory expert; a plain description.

clue.text: Publish octet excitedly following a particular skill in music

indicators.note: following puts the anagram after the lone letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: excitedly shows the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An excited publication of an octet, after a rare musical gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' signals the anagram of the two words; 'following' puts it after the lone A.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect pitch, naming a note without any reference tone, is a rare musical ability.

clue.text: Boost area this month with reinvigoration

indicators.note: reinvigoration suggests the letters are shaken up and given new life in another order

explanation.surface: A regional regeneration push promised for the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reinvigoration' rearranges AREA THIS MONTH; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a stimulus or fillip, from an injection giving a lift, so a boost.

clue.text: Inhabitant supporting workers' representatives in US city

indicators.note: in a down light, supporting means sitting below the other piece

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the UK's federation of trade unions
a son of a place is a native, one who lives there

explanation.surface: A local resident backing union officials in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts SON underneath TUC. The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arizona city near the Mexican border is an example of a city in the United States.

clue.text: Rome had soured around Wednesday? Jump on a return flight

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on either side of the day's letter
soured means the letters of the two words have gone off into a new arrangement

parts.note: to bound is to leap or jump

explanation.surface: A traveller sours on Rome midweek and leaps aboard a flight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soured' makes HOMEARD, and 'around' wraps it round the day's letter. 'Jump' reads as part of the definition but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards one's own house, as a traveller on the flight back is; a descriptive synonym.

clue.text: Camp very warm — work suspended while warmth's accommodated

indicators.note: accommodated means the warmth is housed within what remains
suspended means the work is halted, taken out of the warm word

parts.note: tropical weather is very warm
OP is short for opus, a work
heat is warmth; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A hot holiday camp where activities stop while the heating is put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' leaves TRICAL, and 'accommodated' houses the warmth there. 'Camp' looks like a noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp behaviour is exaggerated and showy, as stagey manners are; a sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Group abandoning final search

indicators.note: abandoning final means the group word loses its last letter

parts.note: a combo is a small band or group of musicians

explanation.surface: A band quits its last search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning final' drops the last letter of COMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: To go carefully through an area looking for something is to search it; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Dispute about cut-down hat and shoe

indicators.note: about puts the quarrel around the shortened hat

parts.note: a set-to is a quarrel or fight

indicators.note: cut-down means the hat word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: An argument over a trimmed hat and a matching pair of shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-down' leaves TIL; 'about' signals the container. Tile for a hat is old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a woman's shoe with a high thin heel; an example of footwear.

clue.text: Classic picture showing lagoon polluted with acid

indicators.note: polluted suggests the letters of the two words are contaminated into a new order

explanation.surface: A painting depicting a lagoon poisoned with acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polluted' rearranges LAGOON ACID; 'showing' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian name for Leonardo's Mona Lisa, the most famous classic painting there is.

clue.text: Canadian city very much distant? Not entirely

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive, too much

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for distant loses its last letter

parts.note: away means distant or absent

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Canadian city is very far off; the answer is: not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims AWAY to AWA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ontario city is Canada's capital, an example of a Canadian city.

clue.text: Good to be in Scottish town, coming back for grouse

indicators.note: coming back means the whole is read from right to left
to be in means the good letter is placed inside the town

parts.note: Elgin is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland

explanation.surface: A good person settles in a Scottish town and returns to shoot grouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' makes ELGGIN; 'coming back' turns it round. 'grouse' is the verb, complain, not the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to grumble, and a small nagging complaint is a niggle; here the noun sense, a gripe.

clue.text: The writer supports orchestra accommodating individual solo

indicators.note: in a down light, supports means sitting below the rest
accommodating means the orchestra letters take in the single one

parts.note: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra
one means a single individual
the writer refers to the setter, who is me

explanation.surface: A writer backs an orchestra that makes room for one player's solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts ONE in LSO; 'supports' places ME beneath in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo as an adjective means on one's own, and feeling solitary and alone is the sense here.

clue.text: Sensational writer, one really impressive (but name's forgotten)

indicators.note: forgotten means the name letter is dropped from the slang word

parts.note: a stonker is British slang for something excellent or impressive
N is the abbreviation for name; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A sensational author whose blockbuster made an impression, though nobody remembers the name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten' removes N from STONKER, British slang for a cracker or stunner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram, author of Dracula, wrote sensational Gothic fiction, so he is an example of such a writer.

clue.text: Dim person accepting a lot of crime, say, not being bright

indicators.note: accepting means the fool takes in the shortened evil

parts.note: a twit is a foolish, dim person

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word for evil, without its last letter

parts.note: a crime is an example of an ill, an evil

explanation.surface: A dim-witted crook takes on plenty of crime without being clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like the definition but goes with 'person'. 'a lot of' cuts ILL to IL; 'accepting' puts it in TWIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit faintly, as at dusk, so lacking brightness; the clue's phrase is an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Confused radio description of ruler's power

indicators.note: radio signals that the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the throne stands for a monarch's sovereign power

explanation.surface: A muddled broadcast describing a monarch's authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radio' calls for a word that sounds like THRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown means being disconcerted or bewildered, an idiomatic synonym for confused.

clue.text: Cabinet presenting combat doctor with honour

parts.note: war is armed combat
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: The government Cabinet decorates an army doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests government ministers, but it is a piece of furniture. The OBE is a British royal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cupboard for hanging clothes is a type of cabinet, a piece of storage furniture.

clue.text: Recreation less ignored by student when college is closed?

parts.note: rec is a short form of recreation

indicators.note: ignored by means the student letter is left out of the word less

parts.note: taken as written
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: Fewer leisure activities overlooked by a student out of term time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored by' signals the deletion, leaving ESS; L for student comes from the learner plate on a British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A break between terms when classes stop is the time a college shuts, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Video game's greeting omitting one line

indicators.note: omitting means one line letter is dropped from the greeting

parts.note: hallo is a variant of hello
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A video game's opening greeting cuts a line of dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting' removes one L from HALLO.
explanation.definitionFit: The science-fiction shooter series from Bungie is a well-known example of a video game.

clue.text: Considerate, proper love — what's very much our thing about that?

indicators.note: about that means the slang phrase goes around the preceding pieces

parts.note: the slang phrase 'so us' means very much our style
licit means lawful, proper
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A caring, decent kind of love: what could be more our style?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about that' wraps the slang phrase round the other two pieces; 'so us' is colloquial for typical of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxiously attentive to someone's welfare is being considerate; a near synonym.

clue.text: Go to carry a platter

indicators.note: to carry means the attempt holds the single letter inside it

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a go at carrying a serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts A inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat dish for carrying or serving food is a platter; a near synonym for a serving board.

clue.text: Founder of attraction reviewed sad museum data

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked over again and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A founder of a tourist draw assesses dismal figures from a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges SAD MUSEUM DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: The French wax modeller started the famous London waxworks, a major visitor attraction.
